newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel attacks Lagardere in Thomson bid battle.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel attacks Lagardere in Thomson bid battle.

text.p: France's Alcatel Alsthom and partner Dassault, launching an offensive in a battle to acquire state-controlled Thomson-CSF, said on Tuesday that victory by rival Lagardere would lead to a break-up of the defence firm.
Alcatel and Dassault said their offer would best preserve French interests by first creating a strong group before opening talks with potential European partners.
The government has so far kept silent on bids for its 58-percent stake in Thomson-CSF and a decision is not due until after June's second round in the French parliamentary elections.

Alcatel and Dassault Industries, which holds a controlling stake in warplane maker Dassault Aviation, are competing with missiles-to-publishing company Lagardere for control of Thomson-CSF in the privatisation race.
Lagardere's Matra defence unit twinned its bid for Thomson-CSF with alliances with British Aerospace Plc and Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA).

Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk told a news conference Lagardere's bid would lead to the break-up of Thomson-CSF, whereas under the Alcatel/Dassault plan the defence electronics group could confidently enter negotiations with European groups such as British Aerospace Plc, GEC Plc or DASA.

"Matra will be forced to enter complex structures in which it will give up majority control to finance an operation which is beyond its means and which will inevitably lead to the break-up of Thomson-CSF," Tchuruk said.
"Our aim is to have a strong French group first and then to start talks with the others," said Dassault's Serge Dassault said at a joint news conference with Tchuruk.
"Otherwise it would come down to taking off your clothes beforehand. That's a bit of what Matra is doing, it's undressing in front of DASA before considering French interests," he said.
Lagardere accused its rivals of using "untruthful arguments" to discredit its bid.

"Who could believe that Lagardere will dismantle Thomson-CSF? Who could believe that Lagardere will not defend -- with great energy -- the French patrimonial interests for which it is responsible?" Lagardere said in a statement that stopped short of an outright denial its bid would break up Thomson-CSF.

If Alcatel and Dassault won the bidding, in which financial details remained undisclosed, they would transfer certain activities to Thomson-CSF, adding 50 percent to its size to give it annual sales of 60 billion francs ($10.5 billion).
Thomson-CSF, with Dassault's Dassault Electronique, would be Europe's number one and the world's number three in radars and electronic counter-measures.
In military communications, the combination of Thomson-CSF and Alcatel would create a world leader ahead of Lockheed Martin Loral of the United States.

In satellites, a combination of Thomson-CSF, Alcatel and France's Aerospatiale would be leader in Europe and number four in the world. In missiles, Aerospatiale and Thomson-CSF would be number two in Europe and fourth on the world market.
Alcatel and Dassault hope state-owned Aerospatiale will join the group after they win Thomson-CSF.
Tchuruk said that with a combined annual research and development budget of 25 billion francs, Thomson-CSF could be a world leader in all its businesses soon after the year 2000.

He said talks with other European firms, including DASA, were unavoidable. "In the future, with the large Thomson-CSF, it will be necessary to deal with DASA and with GEC. That will have to take place in the coming months, we do not have time to wait for years," he told Reuters.

Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot blasted DASA for having concluded a deal with Lagardere before the government's decision was known and he warned this could hurt the Airbus Industrie European passenger jet consortium.

"It should not be the case that the privatisation of Thomson-CSF leads to a weakening of French aerospace," Michot told the Les Echos newspaper. "An alliance against Aerospatiale (is) signing the Airbus death warrant," he said.

The government has said a decision was due before the end of June but after the parliamentary election in two rounds on May 25 and June 1. The opposition Socialist Party has vowed to stop the privatisation of Thomson-CSF.
($ = 5.725 French Francs)
